facts.statement: The genus Sulcusuchus was named in 1990 by Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini and Luis Spalletti.
facts.quote: The type species Sulcusuchus erraini was named in 1990 by Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini and Luis Spalletti.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MLP 88-IV-10-1 was found near Ingeniero Jacobacci in the Coli Toro Formation and consists of a fragmentary lower jaw.
facts.quote: Its holotype, MLP 88-IV-10-1, was found in the Maastrichtian-Danian Coli Toro Formation, near Ingeniero Jacobacci, comprising a fragmentary mandibular ramus.

facts.statement: A more complete specimen, MPEF 650, was found in the La Colonia Formation and includes a half-meter-long lower jaw fragment, skull base, palate, and snout pieces.
facts.quote: The more complete specimen MPEF 650, was uncovered in the middle levels of the La Colonia Formation, which also dates to the Maastrichtian-Danian interval, and consists of a posterior left mandible fragment of about half a meter long with an associated jaw joint condyle of the skull, lower braincase, rear palate and middle snout fragment.

facts.statement: The outer side of the mandible features a trough, a feature that would be exceptional for a crocodile.
facts.quote: The outer side of the mandible shows the trough, which would be exceptional for a crocodile.

facts.statement: Grooves on the mandible and pterygoids may have housed electro-sensitive organs similar to those in modern river-dwelling cetaceans.
facts.quote: The mandibula and pterygoids show grooves that may have housed electro-sensitive organs, similar to modern cetaceans that inhabit estuarine and river locations.

facts.statement: A 2025 report described a Sulcusuchus specimen preserving 95 gastroliths found in the La Colonia Formation.
facts.quote: In 2025, a specimen of Sulcusuchus (MPEF-PV 11698) preserving 95 gastroliths was reported from the middle layers of the La Colonia Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered in Jacobacci, Río Negro province, within the Campanian-age La Colonia Formation.
facts.quote: Su holotipo, MPEF 650, fue descubierto en Jacobacci, en la provincia de Río Negro, en una capa del finales del Campaniense de la Formación La Colonia.

facts.statement: The outer side of the mandible shows a canal, a trait unknown in crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: El lado externo de la mandíbula muestra un canal, un rasgo desconocido en los crocodilomorfos.

facts.statement: The mandible and pterygoids show grooves that may have housed electro-sensitive organs.
facts.quote: La mandíbula y los pterigoideos muestran surcos que pueden haber alojado órganos electro-sensitivos.

facts.statement: The snout is very elongated and the pterygoids are fused.
facts.quote: El hocico es muy alargado y los pterigoideos están fusionados.

facts.statement: Sulcusuchus is classified within the family Polycotylidae.
Sulcusuchus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sulcusuchus is a genus of polycotylid plesiosaur from the Maastrichtian of Argentina.
facts.quote: Sulcusuchus is a genus of polycotylid plesiosaur from the Maastrichtian of Argentina.
